Renaming the Gulf of Mexico as the Gulf of America through H.R. 276 isn’t a “word game” — it’s a sovereignty play. While Congressman Jackson’s focus on wildfire relief and farm bills (like his Livestock Indemnity Program Enhancement Act) is valid, dismissing this rebranding misses the point. Strategic branding reinforces national identity and territorial integrity, which matters when adversaries like China exploit ambiguous terminology to challenge U.S. maritime claims.

That said, Washington’s real failure is prioritizing performative acts over slashing $50B in annual foreign aid or auditing the Pentagon’s $886B budget.

Rename the Gulf? Fine. But stop sending taxpayer cash to Gaza and Kyiv while our ranchers battle wildfires with one hand tied.

The One Big Beautiful Bill Act is exactly the kind of fiscal insanity that proves DC’s priorities are broken. While Musk rightly calls out its deficit explosion, let’s be clear: the real rot is Congress’ addiction to burning $3.8 trillion on pet projects while gutting programs Americans rely on.

Section 278’s AI power grab and Medicaid cuts reveal a system that serves lobbyists, not taxpayers. The House rammed through this monstrosity with zero bipartisan support—typical swamp behavior.

Trump’s DOGE team slashed $170B in waste, but this bill undoes that progress. Bottom line? Both parties keep playing shell games with your money. Time to demand real cuts, not theater.

This isn’t neglect—it’s systemic failure. Chicago’s hospital AC collapses (Weiss Memorial, West Suburban, Community First) reveal a pattern of deferred maintenance while bureaucrats funnel billions into pet projects. Where’s the accountability for infrastructure spending? Taxpayer dollars vanish into “modernization” slush funds while vulnerable patients bake in 90-degree rooms.

The real scandal? These hospitals had years of warnings. Instead of fixing critical systems, D.C. prioritizes foreign aid and redundant programs. When heatwaves hit, patients pay the price.

Cut the globalist waste. Fund American infrastructure FIRST.
